score_1_desc:
<20% of inbound trucks arrive against a pre-booked slot.
>50% of daily volume clusters into a single 2-hour window, causing dock queuing beyond 2 hours.
No designated driver holding area - drivers and helpers congregate at the security gate causing congestion.
Dock-in time is not captured, so it cannot feed downstream GRN turnaround-time (TAT) SLAs.
Slot booking, where it exists, is a manual register entry with no QR/Booking-ID confirmation shared with the vendor ahead of arrival.
score_2_desc:
20-50% slot adherence.
Peak-hour concentration still exceeds 40% of daily volume.
Average vehicle wait time 60-120 minutes.
An informal holding area exists but is not enforced, so congregation at the gate persists.
Dock-in time is logged manually but not used to track GRN TAT.
A digital slot booking exists for under 30% of vendors, without a QR/Booking-ID confirmation shared back to the vendor.
score_3_desc:
50-75% slot adherence via a basic appointment scheduler.
Peak-hour concentration reduced to 25-40%.
Average wait time 30-60 minutes.
A designated driver holding area away from the security gate is marked and used for the majority of vehicles.
Dock-in time is captured and reviewed, but not yet formalized as an SLA input for GRN TAT.
A digital slot booking with a QR/Booking-ID confirmation (D-2 indent leading to a D-1 slot) is shared with 30-60% of vendors ahead of arrival.
score_4_desc:
75-90% slot adherence with system-enforced windows.
Peak-hour concentration under 25%.
Average wait time under 30 minutes.
Adherence tracked daily.
The driver holding area is enforced with signage/marshalling, keeping the security gate clear.
Dock-in time is captured digitally and used as the starting SLA clock for downstream GRN TAT.
Digital slot booking with a QR/Booking-ID confirmation (D-2 indent to D-1 slot) is shared with 60-90% of vendors, scanned at the gate to authenticate arrival.
score_5_desc:
>90% slot adherence with automated vendor notification.
Load spread within +/-10% across all shift hours.
Average wait time under 15 minutes.
The holding area is fully marshalled with real-time occupancy visibility and zero congregation at the security gate.
Dock-in time is system-captured and forms the auditable SLA start-point for GRN TAT, with automated breach alerts.
Digital slot booking with a QR/Booking-ID confirmation (D-2 indent to D-1 slot) is shared with over 90% of vendors and scanned at the gate as the primary authentication step, with zero manual slot entries.

score_1_desc:
<50% of gate entries verified against indent/invoice before unloading starts (across the 70:30 vendor:courier vehicle mix, with no differentiated checklist for vendor vs courier vehicles).
Documentation/invoice mismatch rate above 30%.
Average gate-in time over 20 min/vehicle.
There is no driver-ID or vehicle-number authentication against the booked slot, and temperature checks (where done at all) are not scoped to any specific SKU or deviation threshold.
score_2_desc:
50-70% verified pre-unload, using a single generic checklist applied to both vendor (70% of vehicle mix) and courier (30% of vehicle mix) vehicles.
Mismatch rate 20-30%.
Gate-in time 15-20 min/vehicle.
Driver-ID and vehicle-number are checked against the slot for under 30% of vehicles.
A temperature check is performed inconsistently and without a defined deviation threshold, even for 4°C-sensitive SKUs (e.g., mushrooms).
score_3_desc:
70-85% verified against a defined checklist (vendor, invoice, indented qty, reefer temperature), with separate verification steps for vendor trucks (70% of vehicle mix) and courier vans (30% of vehicle mix).
Mismatch rate 10-20%.
Gate-in time 10-15 min.
Driver-ID and vehicle-number are authenticated against the vendor code, PO, and slot for 30-60% of vehicles.
Temperature is checked specifically for 4°C-sensitive SKUs (e.g., mushrooms) but the reject threshold (e.g., >3°C deviation) is not consistently applied.
score_4_desc:
85-95% verified via system-assisted matching (barcode/OCR) across both vendor (70% of vehicle mix) and courier (30% of vehicle mix) vehicle streams.
Mismatch rate 5-10%.
Gate-in time 5-10 min.
100% of reefer vehicles temperature-logged.
Driver-ID and vehicle-number authentication against vendor code, PO, and slot covers 60-90% of vehicles.
A defined temperature-reject rule (>3°C deviation for 4°C-sensitive SKUs such as mushrooms only, not the full FnV range) is applied consistently.
score_5_desc:
>95% verified end-to-end digitally with zero manual entry, with vendor (70% of vehicle mix) and courier (30% of vehicle mix) streams tracked and matched separately.
Mismatch rate under 5%.
Gate-in time under 5 min.
Full audit trail with automated exception flags.
Driver-ID and vehicle-number authentication against vendor code, PO, and slot covers over 90% of vehicles with zero exceptions.
The >3°C-deviation temperature-reject rule, scoped only to 4°C-sensitive SKUs (e.g., mushrooms), is enforced with zero missed checks and logged as part of the gate audit trail.

score_1_desc:
0% biometric/facial recognition coverage at shift changeovers.
Manual register only, with no zone-wise capturing of manpower entries (e.g., S&G, packing, put-away, dispatch) against warehouse-sizing-based headcount norms.
Unauthorized-entry incidents exceed 60 per month.
score_2_desc:
Under 30% biometric coverage.
Manual plus partial physical checks.
Zone-wise entry counts recorded ad hoc for under 30% of zones, not benchmarked against a sizing-based manpower plan.
Unauthorized-entry incidents 30-60 per month.
score_3_desc:
30-60% facial recognition coverage at main shift changeovers.
Zone-wise manpower entry tracked for 30-60% of zones (e.g., S&G, packing, put-away) against a defined warehouse-sizing-based headcount norm (illustrative only - e.g., ~10 for S&G, ~25 for packing), reviewed periodically rather than daily.
Unauthorized-entry incidents 10-30 per month.
score_4_desc:
60-90% coverage across all shifts and gates.
Zone-wise entry captured and reconciled daily for 60-90% of zones against the warehouse-sizing-based manpower plan, integrated with the attendance system.
Unauthorized-entry incidents under 10 per month, zero incidents in the last quarter.
score_5_desc:
100% facial recognition and physical-check coverage across all shifts and gates.
Zone-wise manpower entry captured in real time for 100% of zones, with automated variance alerts against the warehouse-sizing-based headcount plan.
Zero unauthorized-entry incidents in the last 12 months.
Real-time anomaly alerts.

score_1_desc:
No formal dock allocation.
Dock utilization under 50%.
Docks unnumbered or inconsistently numbered.
score_2_desc:
Manual dock allocation sheet.
Utilization 50-65%.
score_3_desc:
Defined dock allocation by vehicle size with numbered docks.
Utilization 65-80%.
FIFO followed for over 70% of vehicles.
score_4_desc:
System-based dock scheduling with size-matched allocation.
Utilization 80-90%.
FIFO adherence above 90%.
Green-channel vehicles unloaded within 15 minutes.
score_5_desc:
Fully automated dock-vehicle matching with real-time queuing.
Utilization above 90%.
FIFO adherence 100%.
Green-channel wait time under 10 minutes.

score_1_desc:
Under 25% of docks fitted with buffers.
More than 1 dock-damage incident per week.
No penalty framework for drivers causing repeat dock damage.
Physical damage to dock structures (bumpers, levelers, shelters, columns) not tracked or inspected separately from buffer coverage.
score_2_desc:
25-50% buffer coverage.
1 dock-damage incident per week on average.
Repeat-offender drivers flagged informally but no defined penalty applied.
Physical dock-structure damage noted only when reported by staff, with no periodic inspection.
score_3_desc:
50-75% buffer coverage.
1 dock-damage incident every 2 weeks.
A defined penalty (e.g., warning/fine) applied to drivers on a repeat incident.
Physical dock-structure damage inspected monthly and logged separately from buffer-related damage.
score_4_desc:
75-95% buffer coverage.
Fewer than 1 dock-damage incident every 4 weeks.
A graded penalty scale (warning, fine, vendor/transporter review) enforced for repeat-offender drivers.
Periodic buffer-condition audits in place.
Physical dock-structure damage inspected weekly with defects tracked to closure.
score_5_desc:
100% dock buffer coverage.
Zero damage incidents in the last 12 months.
Graded penalty scale for repeat-offender drivers strictly enforced with under 2% repeat-offense rate.
Preventive maintenance schedule tracked.
Zero unresolved physical dock-structure damage, verified via weekly inspection.

score_1_desc:
No defined/target unloading SLA.
No dock-wise dedicated workforce assigned.
No defined palletisation zone (material is palletized wherever space is available, creating space constraints at the inbound gate).
No crate-stacking pattern defined (poor vertical space utilization).
Waste (e.g., vegetable trimmings) accumulates at the entry gate.
No separate lane/green-channel for reliable vendors or for dry-category inbound.
No bypass-routing flag exists for vendor pre-packed material, so pre-packed loads are routed through S&G by default regardless of need.
score_2_desc:
An unloading SLA is defined but tracked for under 30% of docks (benchmark: ~500 units/person/hour for pre-packed material).
Dock-wise workforce assignment is informal.
A palletisation zone is nominally marked but frequently encroached upon.
Crate stacking has no defined SOP.
Waste disposal remains near the inbound gate.
A bypass flag for vendor pre-packed material is used informally for under 30% of eligible loads.
score_3_desc:
Unloading SLA (~500 units/person/hour pre-packed) is tracked for 30-60% of docks with a dock-wise supervisor-led team.
A visibly marked palletisation zone and sorting/grading area are maintained on most days.
A crate-stacking SOP (max stack height, brick/inline pattern) is defined but followed inconsistently.
A green channel exists for some reliable vendors.
Waste disposal has been relocated away from the inbound gate.
A bypass-routing flag for vendor pre-packed material, skipping S&G and routing straight to packing/staging, is applied for 30-60% of eligible loads.
score_4_desc:
Unloading SLA is tracked for 60-90% of docks against benchmark, with a dock-wise supervisor-led team on every shift.
Palletisation zone, unloading area, and S&G area are marked and adhered to.
Crate-stacking SOP is followed on 70-95% of pallets.
A green channel is consistently used for reliable vendors.
FIFO lanes for S&G are marked on the floor.
Dry-category inbound has a defined separate lane.
The bypass-routing flag for vendor pre-packed material is applied for 60-90% of eligible loads, tracked as part of the load-declaration step at gate/weighment.
score_5_desc:
Unloading SLA is tracked for over 90% of docks and consistently meets/exceeds the ~500 units/person/hour benchmark, with a dock-wise supervisor-led team at all times.
Palletisation zone, unloading area, and S&G area are marked, audited, and adhered to with zero space-constraint incidents.
Crate-stacking SOP compliance exceeds 95%.
Green-channel and dry-category lanes operate with zero cross-flow incidents.
Waste is cleared from a defined point on a fixed schedule.
The bypass-routing flag for vendor pre-packed material is applied for over 90% of eligible loads with zero mis-routes, fully integrated into the load-declaration and GRN-generation step.

score_1_desc:
Weighment data is logged manually for GRN/PO creation - error-prone and slow.
Weighment occurs downstream of S&G, increasing vendor wait time and delaying PO closure.
The weighment area sits hard against the staging area with no clear aisle, creating a choke point.
Scale calibration is untracked.
score_2_desc:
Manual logging accounts for over 70% of weighment transactions.
Weighment is still performed post-S&G for the majority of vehicles.
The clear aisle between weighment and staging is under 1.5m or undefined.
Scale calibration is done ad hoc with no fixed schedule.
score_3_desc:
Digital weighment is integrated with the WMS/GRN system for 30-60% of transactions.
Weighment has been shifted to the unloading stage for some vendor categories, reducing PO-closure delay.
A minimum 1.5m clear aisle between weighment and staging is maintained on most days.
Scales are calibrated on a defined but not strictly daily schedule.
score_4_desc:
Digital weighment integrated with WMS/GRN covers 60-90% of transactions.
Weighment is performed at the unloading stage for the majority of vendors, ahead of S&G.
The 1.5m clear-aisle buffer between weighment and staging is consistently maintained.
Calibrated scales with tare memory per packaging type are recalibrated on a defined schedule (daily recommended).
Digital weight logs are retained as an audit trail.
score_5_desc:
Over 90% of weighment transactions are digitally integrated with WMS/GRN with zero manual entry.
Weighment is performed at the unloading stage for all applicable vendors, enabling same-day PO closure.
The 1.5m clear-aisle buffer is maintained with zero choke-point incidents.
Scales are recalibrated daily with tare memory per packaging type.
The digital weight log is used as a routine audit trail for supplier invoice reconciliation and shrinkage analysis.

score_1_desc:
Gate operates as a security checkpoint, not a capacity-gated release valve: trucks are waved onto the dock/yard regardless of whether a dock bay or staging space is available, with no reject / temp-reject / hold / bypass decision rule (checks vary guard-to-guard).
Gate-out has no exit slip or outbound-seal verification. Vehicles routinely block the dock and back up into S&G congestion.
score_2_desc:
A capacity check is attempted informally for under 30% of gate-ins (e.g., a phone call to the dock supervisor) with no defined time window, so vehicles sent to hold still cause dock-blocking regularly.
Reject/hold decisions depend on individual guard judgment.
Gate-out has no formal exit slip or seal check.
score_3_desc:
A defined capacity check (dock bay + staging pallet positions available within a stated window, e.g., 15 minutes) gates 30-60% of gate-ins, routing 'no' decisions to the holding area.
A basic reject-vs-hold rule exists, but temp-reject (scoped to 4°C SKUs) and bypass-routing (pre-packed vendors) are not yet part of the same decision rule.
Gate-out issues an exit slip for the majority of dispatches but outbound-seal verification is inconsistent.
score_4_desc:
Capacity-gated release (dock bay + staging space confirmed within 15 minutes) governs 60-90% of gate-ins.
The full reject / temp-reject / hold / bypass decision taxonomy is defined and applied consistently, with 'hold' vehicles routed to the designated holding area.
Gate-out issues an exit slip and verifies the outbound vehicle seal for the majority of dispatches.
Physical enablers (multi-lane entry, boom barrier, CCTV/tablet at the gate) are in place.
score_5_desc:
Over 90% of gate-ins are capacity-gated in real time (dock bay + staging space confirmed within 15 minutes, tied live to the dock-management and staging systems), with zero blind releases and zero dock-blocking incidents.
The full reject / temp-reject / hold / bypass decision taxonomy is applied with a complete audit trail.
Gate-out is fully controlled (exit slip plus outbound-seal verification on 100% of dispatches).
Physical enablers (multi-lane entry with boom barrier, CCTV/tablet, and weighbridge where applicable) are fully deployed.

score_1_desc: Dock-to-Stock Time (vehicle arrival to inventory available) exceeds 8 hours on average, with no visibility into which stage (dock-in, GRN, or putaway) drives the delay.
score_2_desc: Dock-to-Stock Time averages 5-8 hours.
score_3_desc: Dock-to-Stock Time averages 3-5 hours, tracked as a single facility-level number without a stage-wise breakdown.
score_4_desc: Dock-to-Stock Time averages 1.5-3 hours, broken down by dock-in, GRN TAT, and putaway TAT to flag the slowest stage.
score_5_desc: Dock-to-Stock Time is held under 1.5 hours on average, tracked in real time end-to-end (dock-in -> GRN TAT -> putaway TAT) with automated stage-wise breach alerts.

score_1_desc: Unloading TAT (dock-in to unloading-complete) exceeds 90 minutes per vehicle on average.
score_2_desc: Unloading TAT averages 60-90 minutes per vehicle.
score_3_desc: Unloading TAT averages 40-60 minutes per vehicle, tracked per vehicle for the majority of dock-ins.
score_4_desc: Unloading TAT averages 25-40 minutes per vehicle, tracked per vehicle and reviewed daily against the unloading SLA.
score_5_desc: Unloading TAT is held under 25 minutes per vehicle for over 90% of dock-ins, tracked in real time and feeding the Dock-to-Stock Time KPI.

score_1_desc: Putaway TAT (GRN complete to putaway complete) exceeds 6 hours, so goods sit unavailable to pick for most of a shift after GRN posting.
score_2_desc: Putaway TAT averages 4-6 hours.
score_3_desc: Putaway TAT averages 2-4 hours, tracked daily by zone.
score_4_desc: Putaway TAT averages 1-2 hours, tracked daily by zone/SKU against a defined target.
score_5_desc: Putaway TAT is held under 1 hour for over 90% of GRNs, tracked in real time by zone/SKU, closing the loop from GRN completion to pick-availability and feeding the Dock-to-Stock Time KPI.

score_1_desc: 0-2 of the 9 core QMS elements (policy, objectives, SOPs, exception handling, responsibility matrix, escalation matrix, risk analysis, complaints/feedback loop, documentation control) are documented.
score_2_desc:
3-4 elements documented.
No formal review cycle in place.
score_3_desc:
5-6 elements documented and in active use.
Reviewed annually.
score_4_desc: 7-8 elements documented, tracked, and reviewed quarterly with defined ownership.
score_5_desc: All 9 elements fully documented, version-controlled, reviewed quarterly, and linked to a closed-loop CAPA process with under 5-day average closure time.

score_1_desc:
No defined sampling percentage or rejection threshold.
Inspection is ad hoc, covering under 5% of inbound lots.
GRN is raised and approved without any dependency on a quality-check procedure or quality-team clearance.
Acceptance/rejection is based purely on visual inspection with no structured Arrival Quality Report (AQR) or fixed cutoff defined before unloading begins, and QC/vehicle rejection rates are not tracked by vendor or SKU.
score_2_desc:
Sampling done on 5-10% of lots, but rejection threshold undefined or inconsistently applied.
GRN approval nominally requires quality-team sign-off, but this is often obtained after goods are already put away, not before GRN posting.
A written AQR format exists but fixed sampling/defect cutoffs are not consistently applied before unloading starts.
Rejection data is recorded but not segmented by vendor or SKU.
score_3_desc:
Sampling fixed at approximately 10% of received quantity.
Rejection threshold set at 20% defect rate for full-lot rejection, but not segmented by SKU/category.
GRN approval is procedurally linked to quality-team clearance, but clearance is manual/paper-based and not enforced as a system hold.
A defined AQR is used for the majority of lots (e.g., 10% sampling, reject lot if defect >20%), completed before unloading begins.
QC reject % and vehicle rejection % are tracked in aggregate but not yet split by vendor/SKU for a supplier scorecard.
score_4_desc:
10% sampling and 20% rejection threshold applied and segmented by category (FnV vs dry), with batch/expiry and 70-80% shelf-life checks enforced.
GRN cannot be posted until the quality team records clearance against the defined inspection procedure.
AQR with fixed sampling/defect cutoffs is completed before unloading starts for 85-95% of lots.
QC reject % and vehicle rejection % are tracked by vendor and SKU and feed a periodic supplier scorecard.
score_5_desc:
Sampling and rejection norms (10%/20%) defined per SKU category, digitally logged, with under 2% inspection-error rate and monthly trend analysis on rejection causes.
GRN approval is system-enforced with zero exceptions, released only on digital quality-team clearance against the defined procedure, with a full audit trail of inspector sign-off.
AQR is completed before unloading begins for over 95% of lots with zero exceptions.
QC reject % and vehicle rejection % by vendor and SKU are tracked in real time and drive an automated, continuously updated supplier scorecard used in vendor review.

score_1_desc:
No defined return-to-vendor (RTV) policy.
Under 30% of returns closed same-day.
score_2_desc:
Informal RTV process.
30-50% same-day closure.
score_3_desc:
RTV policy defined by SKU category (hard/soft).
50-75% same-day closure.
score_4_desc:
RTV policy defined and tracked.
75-95% same-day closure.
Space occupied by pending returns reviewed weekly.
score_5_desc:
RTV fully systemized.
Over 95% same-day closure.
Zero aged-return inventory beyond 24 hours.

score_1_desc:
Complaint rate exceeds 3% of FnV volume handled, or is not tracked at all.
Complaint density is not tracked in PPM at all, or exceeds 500 PPM where estimated, so order-level density cannot be benchmarked against a quick-commerce/dark-store standard.
score_2_desc:
Complaint rate tracked at 2.5-3%, with no root-cause analysis.
Complaints PPM runs at 200-500, calculated only occasionally/retrospectively.
score_3_desc:
Complaint rate at the typical industry band of 2-2.5%, tracked monthly with basic categorization.
Complaints PPM runs at 100-200, tracked monthly alongside the %-of-volume metric.
score_4_desc:
Complaint rate reduced to 1-2%, with root-cause analysis and corrective actions closed within 7 days.
Complaints PPM runs at 50-100, tracked weekly against a defined benchmark band.
score_5_desc:
Complaint rate under 1% (best-in-class), with real-time tracking, root-cause analysis, and closed-loop resolution within 48 hours.
Complaints PPM is held under 50 (best-in-class), tracked daily against benchmark, giving both a wholesale (volume-based) and dark-store/quick-commerce (order-based) view of complaint density.

score_1_desc: Near-miss/safety incidents are not logged at all, or exceed 5 per week where informally counted.
score_2_desc: 3-5 near-miss/safety incidents occur per week, logged reactively (typically only after a reportable injury).
score_3_desc: 1-3 near-miss/safety incidents occur per week, logged daily but reviewed only monthly with no corrective-action tracking.
score_4_desc: Under 1 near-miss/safety incident per week, logged and reviewed daily with corrective actions tracked to closure for the majority of incidents.
score_5_desc: Zero reportable safety incidents and under 1 near-miss per month, logged and reviewed daily with corrective actions closed within a defined SLA.

score_1_desc: Ongoing chiller/freezer temperature compliance (beyond the inbound gate check in A1.2) is not monitored, or runs under 70% where spot-checked.
score_2_desc: Compliance runs at 70-85%, based on a few manual spot-checks a day.
score_3_desc: Compliance runs at 85-95%, logged daily via manual readings for the main cold zones.
score_4_desc: Compliance runs at 95-98%, logged continuously via sensors for the majority of cold-chain zones with daily breach review.
score_5_desc: Compliance exceeds 98%, monitored continuously via sensors across 100% of cold-chain zones with real-time breach alerts.

score_1_desc:
No formal 5S audit.
Audit score under 40% where measured at all.
No physical demarcation of aisles, S&G/packing areas, storage space, buffer-pallet staging, packaging-material storage, or tools/machinery locations - floor markings, if any, are inconsistent or absent.
No designated area/zone name signage, fire extinguisher position signage, or fire exit signage is installed anywhere in the facility.
score_2_desc:
5S introduced in a pilot area only.
Audit score 40-55%.
Floor marking/demarcation done for under 30% of the required zones (aisles, S&G/packing spaces, storage, buffer-pallet staging, packaging material, tools/machinery), and only in the pilot area.
Signage exists for a few zones and fire extinguisher points only, limited to the pilot area; fire exits are marked but not consistently visible or illuminated.
score_3_desc:
Sort/Set/Shine implemented facility-wide.
Audit score 55-70%.
Audits conducted quarterly.
Demarcation in place for 30-60% of required zones - e.g., aisles and storage racking are marked, but S&G/packing space, buffer-pallet staging, packaging-material, and tools/machinery locations are only partially marked.
Designated area signage and fire extinguisher position signage are installed for 30-60% of required zones/points; fire exits are signed and illuminated for the main escape routes only.
score_4_desc:
Standardized across all zones with monthly audits.
Score 70-85%.
Training conducted at least twice a year.
Demarcation covers 60-90% of required zones, including aisles, S&G and packing space boundaries, storage space marking, buffer-pallet staging area, and packaging-material storage, with tools/machinery locations marked but not yet audited on a fixed schedule.
Area signage, fire extinguisher signage, and fire exit signage cover 60-90% of required zones/points/routes, checked alongside the periodic 5S review.
score_5_desc:
5S sustained for over 12 months.
Audit score above 85%.
Daily checks, biannual training, and a documented continuous-improvement (Kaizen) count.
100% of zones demarcated and colour-coded - aisles, S&G and packing spaces, storage space, buffer-pallet staging, packaging-material storage, and tools/machinery locations - with demarcation adherence audited as part of the daily 5S check.
100% of zones carry designated area signage, every fire extinguisher position is signed, and all fire exits/escape routes are signed, illuminated, and unobstructed - verified as part of the daily 5S and safety audit.

score_1_desc:
0-1 of the 5 lean principles (value definition, value stream mapping, flow, pull, continuous improvement) deployed.
No PDCA or waste tracking.
score_2_desc:
2 principles deployed (e.g., value stream mapping started).
PDCA used in under 20% of processes.
score_3_desc:
3 principles deployed.
PDCA embedded in 20-50% of processes.
2-3 of the 8 waste types tracked.
score_4_desc:
4 principles deployed with pull/JIT replenishment active.
PDCA in 50-80% of processes.
5-6 of the 8 waste types tracked with quarterly reduction targets.
score_5_desc:
All 5 principles fully embedded.
PDCA in over 80% of processes.
All 8 waste types tracked with measurable year-on-year reduction of over 10%.

score_1_desc: Under 30% of standard and exception scenarios documented in SOPs.
score_2_desc:
30-50% documented.
Exception flows largely undocumented.
score_3_desc: 50-75% documented, including major exception scenarios.
score_4_desc: 75-95% documented and version-controlled, reviewed twice a year.
score_5_desc: Over 95% of scenarios (standard ITL plus exceptions) documented, digitized, and reviewed quarterly, with zero undocumented recurring exceptions.

score_1_desc:
No defined size or quality standards (blemish-free, rot-free, infestation-free) for sorting/grading.
Criteria applied on 0% of SKUs.
No S&G throughput SLA is defined (benchmark: ~70 units/person/hour for general S&G, 400-500 units/person/shift for leafy cutting).
Piece-category SKUs (e.g., coconut, watermelon) are staffed randomly, causing significant throughput slowdown.
score_2_desc:
Standards defined for under 30% of SKUs.
A throughput SLA is defined but tracked for under 30% of stations, with wide variance against the ~70 units/person/hour / 400-500 units/person/shift benchmarks.
Piece-category SKUs are not assigned to experienced manpower.
score_3_desc:
Standards defined for 30-60% of SKUs, covering blemish, rot, infestation, and size checks.
Throughput SLA (~70 units/person/hour, 400-500/shift for leafy) is tracked for 30-60% of stations.
Experienced manpower is assigned to piece-category SKUs (coconut, watermelon) only inconsistently.
score_4_desc:
Standards defined for 60-90% of SKUs, with grading accuracy audited monthly at over 90% accuracy.
Throughput SLA is tracked for 60-90% of stations, mostly within benchmark.
Experienced manpower is consistently assigned to piece-category SKUs, limiting their drag on overall S&G throughput.
score_5_desc:
Standards defined for 100% of SKUs.
Grading accuracy above 95%, audited weekly with a corrective feedback loop.
Throughput SLA is tracked for 100% of stations and consistently meets or exceeds benchmark (~70 units/person/hour, 400-500/shift leafy).
Piece-category SKUs are always staffed with experienced manpower, with throughput impact monitored and minimized.

score_1_desc:
Packing productivity under 60 units/person/hour.
Packaging material (nets/boxes/LDP) not defined by SKU.
No shift-level SLA is tracked against the net/box/shrink packing benchmarks (~900-1,000 net, ~1,100-1,200 box, ~1,000-1,100 shrink units/person/shift).
Formed boxes are stacked directly on the worktop causing clutter.
Vendor-packed SKUs are routinely re-packed on arrival.
Chilled-category SKUs (e.g., apples, pears) are packed under ambient conditions with no dedicated chilled station.
score_2_desc:
Productivity 60-80 units/person/hour.
Packaging material defined for under 50% of SKUs.
Shift-level SLA is tracked for under 30% of lines against the net/box/shrink benchmarks.
A formed-box staging shelf is used on under 30% of lines.
Vendor-pack alignment to FC standards covers under 30% of applicable vendors.
Chilled SKUs are packed ambient on over 70% of shifts.
score_3_desc:
Productivity at the 80-100 units/person/hour benchmark band.
Packaging material defined per SKU.
Shift-level SLA is tracked for 30-60% of lines and trending toward the net/box/shrink benchmarks.
A formed-box staging shelf decongests the worktop on 30-60% of lines.
30-60% of applicable vendors pack to FC standard, removing the re-pack step.
A dedicated chilled packing station is used for 30-60% of chilled-SKU shifts.
score_4_desc:
Productivity 100-120 units/person/hour, matching category benchmarks (net roll ~90/hr, pannet ~100/hr, LDP ~100/hr).
Gang output tracked daily against a 400-500 packets/person/day target.
Shift-level SLA is tracked for 60-90% of lines and mostly at benchmark (~900-1,200 units/person/shift by pack type).
Formed-box staging shelf standard is followed on 60-90% of lines.
60-90% of applicable vendors pack to FC standard.
A dedicated chilled packing station is used for 60-90% of chilled-SKU shifts.
score_5_desc:
Productivity above 120 units/person/hour or consistently at the top of the category benchmark.
A 4-cutter + 6-packer gang achieving 4,000+ packets/day, tracked and improved monthly.
Shift-level SLA is tracked for over 90% of lines and consistently at or above benchmark.
Formed-box staging shelf standard is followed on all lines.
Over 90% of applicable vendors pack to FC standard with zero re-pack sub-process.
100% of chilled SKUs are packed at a dedicated chilled station, tracked and improved monthly.

score_1_desc:
No standard manpower norm for processing tables.
Occupancy varies randomly (under 2 or over 6 people per 8ft x 4ft table).
No defined ratio of S&G tables to packaging tables - S&G tables are frequently fewer than packing tables, bottlenecking downstream packaging input.
No cleaning step is enforced between vendors' S&G batches, causing clutter and cross-contamination risk.
score_2_desc:
Norm defined (4 people per 8ft x 4ft table) but followed on under 40% of tables.
An S&G-to-packing table ratio is loosely followed for under 40% of shifts, with S&G output frequently under-matched to packing input.
Inter-vendor cleaning is ad hoc.
score_3_desc:
4-person-per-table norm followed on 40-70% of tables.
S&G-to-packing table ratio is matched to keep S&G output aligned with packing input on 40-70% of shifts.
Cleaning between vendors' S&G batches is performed inconsistently.
score_4_desc:
Norm followed on 70-95% of tables, monitored via regular floor walks.
S&G-to-packing table ratio and output-input matching is maintained on 70-95% of shifts, monitored via floor walks.
Cleaning after each vendor's S&G batch is standard practice.
score_5_desc:
Norm followed on over 95% of tables at all times, with real-time floor supervision preventing congestion or under-utilization.
S&G-to-packing table ratio and output-input matching is maintained on over 95% of shifts with real-time supervision.
Cleaning after every vendor's S&G batch is enforced with zero cross-contamination incidents.

score_1_desc:
Shrinkage not tracked by SKU category.
Overall loss exceeds 5% with no seasonal breakup.
score_2_desc:
Shrinkage tracked in aggregate only.
No category-specific targets (e.g., leafy items vs vegetables like brinjal).
score_3_desc:
Shrinkage tracked by category against benchmark ranges (up to 30-35% for leafy items, 1-2% for vegetables like brinjal).
Seasonal RTV loss tracked at a 1.5-3% band (winter to monsoon).
score_4_desc:
Shrinkage within benchmark for over 80% of SKU categories.
Seasonal loss trend reviewed monthly with corrective action for outliers.
score_5_desc:
Shrinkage consistently at or below benchmark for all categories.
Seasonal loss held at 1.5% or below even during monsoon.
Monthly root-cause review with documented reduction actions.

score_1_desc:
Repacking/re-stickering rate not measured.
Anecdotally exceeds 8% of units reworked.
Cause coding does not distinguish avoidable rework such as re-sorting already vendor-packed bananas at the packing stage, ripeness-based segregation (e.g., mango, avocado) being performed late at the packing stage instead of at S&G, or idle organic-table capacity - all of which inflate the repack rate.
score_2_desc:
Measured but no target set.
Rate at 5-8%.
Rate is measured in aggregate without cause coding for these specific drivers (banana re-sort, late ripeness segregation, idle organic-table capacity).
score_3_desc:
Target set at 5% or below.
Actual performance running at 5-6%.
Cause coding identifies banana re-sort, late ripeness segregation, and idle organic-table time as contributors, but corrective action (stopping banana re-sort, moving ripeness segregation to the S&G stage, converting the organic table to multi-use) is applied inconsistently.
score_4_desc:
Actual rate 2-5%, tracked weekly with cause coding.
Banana re-sort at packing is eliminated, ripeness-based segregation is performed at the S&G stage, and the organic table is run as a time-clustered multi-use table on 70-95% of shifts, reflected in the weekly cause-coded repack trend.
score_5_desc:
Rate under 2%, tracked daily, root cause eliminated at source (labeling/QC), sustained for 2+ consecutive quarters.
Banana re-sort at packing is fully eliminated, ripeness-based segregation is performed at the S&G stage on 100% of shifts, and the organic table is consistently run as a multi-use table in downtime, sustained for 2+ consecutive quarters as a root-cause-eliminated driver of the sub-2% repack rate.

score_1_desc: Packing accuracy (units/cases packed with the correct SKU, quantity, and label) is below 96%, not tracked distinctly from piece-level packing checks.
score_2_desc: Packing accuracy runs at 96-97%, tracked in aggregate only.
score_3_desc: Packing accuracy runs at 97-98%, tracked per packer/shift for the majority of lines.
score_4_desc: Packing accuracy runs at 98-99%, tracked per packer/shift and reviewed daily.
score_5_desc: Packing accuracy exceeds 99%, tracked per packer/shift in real time.

score_1_desc:
0-1 of the 5 demand-planning layers (baseline/historical, seasonal & festive, event-based/sales, time-of-day, area/hyperlocal behavior) in use.
Forecast accuracy under 60%.
Hourly-volatility and SKU-level inaccuracy are not analyzed, and new-store locations run on no meaningful demand data (pure guesswork).
score_2_desc:
2 layers active.
Forecast accuracy 60-75%.
Hourly volatility and hyperlocal (area-level) variation are acknowledged but not modeled.
New stores use a flat citywide/category average with no ramp-up curve.
score_3_desc:
3 layers active (e.g., baseline + seasonal/festive + event-based).
Forecast accuracy 75-85%.
Time-of-day demand curves are tracked for under 50% of SKUs/stores.
Hyperlocal (area-behavior) variation is factored in for high-volume stores only.
New stores follow a defined but generic ramp-up curve.
score_4_desc:
4 of the 5 layers active (typically missing time-of-day or area-behavior).
Forecast accuracy 85-95%.
Time-of-day and hyperlocal demand patterns are modeled for 70-90% of stores.
SKU-level forecast error is tracked and root-caused monthly.
New-store data gaps are bridged with a comparable-store proxy model for the first 4-6 weeks.
score_5_desc:
All 5 layers active and continuously calibrated against actuals (baseline, seasonal/festive, event-based, time-of-day, hyperlocal/area-behavior).
Forecast accuracy above 95%, directly driving the fill-rate KPI.
Hourly volatility and SKU-level accuracy are tracked in real time with automated recalibration.
New-store demand gaps are closed within 2-4 weeks via a proxy-to-actual transition model.

score_1_desc:
0-1 of the 5 inventory-planning components (regular+buffer stock, seasonal buffer of +15-20%, festive buffer of +50-100%, FEFO discipline for fresh/perishable SKUs, SKU assortment) defined.
Stockout/excess (waste) incidents affect over 20% of SKUs monthly.
Batch/expiry tracking is manual or absent, and shelf-life-driven markdowns/write-offs are not visible until after the fact.
score_2_desc:
2 components defined.
Incidents affect 10-20% of SKUs monthly.
FEFO is followed inconsistently, with batch mismanagement (wrong batch picked/dispatched) as a regular occurrence.
Inventory visibility lags actual stock by more than a day.
score_3_desc:
3 components defined (e.g., regular+buffer stock, one of seasonal/festive buffer, and a defined SKU assortment).
Incidents affect 5-10% of SKUs monthly.
FEFO is enforced for the majority of fresh SKUs.
Batch-level visibility exists but is not real-time, creating an occasional stockout-vs-waste trade-off at the shelf-life boundary.
score_4_desc:
4 of the 5 components defined and reviewed monthly (seasonal +15-20% and festive +50-100% buffers both applied, FEFO enforced for fresh).
Incidents affect under 5% of SKUs monthly.
Batch/expiry data is visible near-real-time, keeping the stockout-vs-waste trade-off and batch mismanagement to isolated exceptions.
score_5_desc:
All 5 components defined, automated, and reviewed weekly (regular+buffer stock, seasonal +15-20% buffer, festive +50-100% buffer, FEFO for fresh, SKU assortment).
Incidents affect under 2% of SKUs monthly.
Batch/expiry visibility is real-time and system-enforced, eliminating batch mismanagement and holding the stockout-vs-waste trade-off within a defined tolerance.

score_1_desc:
Replenishment triggered manually and irregularly.
No defined formula (Forecast Demand + Safety Stock - Current Inventory) or wave structure.
No min-max or reorder-point model is defined, no emergency top-up process exists for stockout risk, and days-of-inventory (DoI) is not tracked.
Partial fulfillment, dock congestion at replenishment receipt, and storage overflow are common and unmanaged.
score_2_desc:
Formula-based replenishment defined but run less than once a day.
Wave split ad hoc.
A min-max or reorder-point trigger is defined for under 30% of SKUs.
Emergency top-up is handled ad hoc with no defined SLA.
DoI is tracked in aggregate only.
Partial fulfillment and storage overflow incidents are frequent.
score_3_desc:
Replenishment run once a day using the standard formula.
Wave timing not optimized.
Min-max/reorder-point triggers cover 30-60% of SKUs.
A defined but manually-invoked emergency top-up process exists.
DoI is tracked by category.
Dock congestion from replenishment receipts is reviewed but not systematically avoided.
score_4_desc:
Replenishment run twice a day with a defined wave split (e.g., 70% first wave / 30% second wave).
Lead time and buffer capacity factored in.
Min-max/reorder-point triggers cover 60-90% of SKUs with an SLA-bound emergency top-up process.
DoI is tracked by SKU against a target band.
Dock-congestion and storage-overflow incidents from replenishment receipt are reduced to isolated exceptions.
score_5_desc:
Fully automated twice-daily (or more frequent) replenishment cycle with an optimized wave split (e.g., 70/30), lead-time-adjusted safety stock, and under 2% stockout rate at dark stores.
Min-max/reorder-point triggers cover over 90% of SKUs, integrated with an automated, SLA-bound emergency top-up process (ARS).
DoI is tracked by SKU in real time against target bands.
Dock congestion and storage overflow from replenishment receipts are eliminated through slotted receiving.
Partial-fulfillment incidents are root-caused monthly.

score_1_desc:
0-2 of 6 roles (inbound, outbound/picking, packing, put-away, supervisory, security) have defined manpower planning.
Staffing variance exceeds 20%.
No surge-planning mechanism for demand spikes and no defined gig-workforce flexibility strategy.
Staffing decisions ignore diurnal (hour-of-day) demand variability, and attrition/gig-supply risk are not tracked.
score_2_desc:
3 roles planned.
Staffing variance 15-20%.
Surge planning is reactive (arranged only after a spike is already underway).
Gig-workforce usage is ad hoc with no defined flex ratio.
Diurnal variability is acknowledged but not built into shift design.
Attrition is tracked but not analyzed.
score_3_desc:
4 roles planned.
Variance 10-15%.
A surge-planning trigger and a defined gig-to-permanent flex ratio exist for under 60% of shifts.
Shift design accounts for diurnal variability for the main peak window only.
Attrition and gig-supply risk are tracked monthly without a mitigation plan.
score_4_desc:
5 roles planned with shift-level granularity.
Variance 5-10%.
Surge planning and a defined gig-flex ratio are applied on 60-90% of shifts, with shift design built around the full diurnal demand curve.
Attrition and gig-supply risk are tracked with an active mitigation/backup-pool plan.
score_5_desc:
All 6 roles planned with daily granularity and capacity buffers.
Variance under 5%.
Surge planning and gig-flex ratio are applied on over 90% of shifts with capacity buffers pre-built into the roster.
Shift design is fully diurnal-curve-driven.
Attrition is held below a defined benchmark and gig-supply risk is mitigated via a pre-qualified backup pool, reviewed monthly.

score_1_desc:
Fewer than 1 planned warehouse-to-dark-store replenishment cycle per day.
Dispatch is ad hoc.
No route optimization or truck-load optimization is applied (vehicles dispatched part-full or on unoptimized routes).
No formal pick-path design exists, causing inefficient in-warehouse travel.
Freezer/cold-chain capacity limits are not factored into network planning.
Inbound to not-yet-live (pre-live) dark stores is unplanned and causes downstream issues.
score_2_desc:
1 cycle per day.
Wave split not defined.
Route/truck-load optimization is applied to under 30% of dispatch routes.
Pick-path design is undefined, with operators walking ad hoc.
Freezer-capacity constraints are identified only after a breach.
Pre-live-store inward is handled the same as live-store inward with no distinction.
score_3_desc:
1-2 cycles per day with a defined split (approximately 70/30), but adherence under 70%.
Route/truck-load optimization covers 30-60% of dispatch routes.
A basic pick-path layout exists but is not distance-optimized.
Freezer/cold-chain capacity is checked before dispatch for temperature-sensitive SKUs only.
Pre-live dark-store inward follows a separate but informal process.
score_4_desc:
2 cycles per day with a 70/30 (or optimized) split.
Adherence 70-90%.
Route/truck-load optimization covers 60-90% of dispatch routes, holding OPH (orders-per-hour) close to target.
Pick-path design is distance-optimized and reviewed periodically.
Freezer/cold-chain capacity is planned ahead of dispatch across all temperature zones.
Pre-live dark-store inward follows a defined, separate SOP.
score_5_desc:
2 or more cycles per day, wave-split adherence above 90%, dynamically adjusted to dark-store stock positions in real time.
Route/truck-load optimization covers over 90% of dispatch routes with OPH consistently at or above target.
Pick-path design is continuously optimized using movement data.
Freezer/cold-chain capacity is dynamically planned with zero temperature-zone breaches.
Pre-live dark-store inward is fully governed by a dedicated SOP with zero cross-over incidents into live operations.

score_1_desc:
Fill rate under 70%.
No defined D-minus planning day.
score_2_desc:
Fill rate 70-80%.
D-minus planning cycle used inconsistently.
score_3_desc:
Fill rate 80-90%.
D-minus planning day formally defined and followed for FnV/dry categories.
score_4_desc:
Fill rate 90-95%.
D-minus cycle followed consistently, with variance root-caused monthly.
score_5_desc: Fill rate above 95% (benchmark), D-minus planning followed on 100% of days, over/under-planning variance under 5%.

score_1_desc:
Supplier performance (quality variability, lead-time risk, price volatility, OTIF - on-time-in-full) is not tracked in any structured way.
Sourcing decisions are made without visibility into any of these four dimensions.
OTIF is neither defined nor measured.
score_2_desc:
One of the four dimensions (typically OTIF or price) is tracked in aggregate, with no vendor-level or SKU-level breakdown.
Quality variability and lead-time risk are known anecdotally but not measured.
score_3_desc:
2-3 of the four dimensions are tracked by vendor (e.g., OTIF % and lead-time variance), reviewed periodically (e.g., quarterly), but not yet linked to sourcing/allocation decisions.
Price volatility is monitored but not hedged or contracted against.
score_4_desc:
All four dimensions (quality variability, lead-time risk, price volatility, OTIF) are tracked by vendor and reviewed monthly, feeding a basic supplier scorecard.
Sourcing allocation is adjusted for chronic OTIF/quality underperformers.
Price volatility is partially managed via defined contracting/hedging for key SKUs.
score_5_desc:
All four dimensions are tracked by vendor and SKU in real time via an automated supplier scorecard, directly driving sourcing/allocation decisions and vendor tiering.
OTIF is held above a defined benchmark (e.g., 95%+).
Price volatility is actively hedged/contracted for the majority of high-value categories, with quarterly vendor business reviews closing the loop on quality and lead-time risk.

score_1_desc: Indent is not reconciled against actual inward/dispatch at all, or the variance exceeds 30% where checked.
score_2_desc: Indent-vs-actual variance runs at 20-30%, reconciled only in aggregate.
score_3_desc: Indent-vs-actual variance runs at 10-20%, reconciled daily for the majority of SKUs/stores.
score_4_desc: Indent-vs-actual variance runs at 5-10%, reconciled daily with root cause reviewed monthly.
score_5_desc: Indent-vs-actual variance is held under 5%, reconciled in real time and reported as a standing indent-accuracy KPI alongside forecast accuracy.

score_1_desc: FIFO compliance for inventory rotation (distinct from the dock-sequencing FIFO in A1.4) runs under 50%, with picking/putaway routinely bypassing the oldest-stock-first rule.
score_2_desc: FIFO compliance runs at 50-70%, followed inconsistently across zones.
score_3_desc: FIFO compliance runs at 70-85%, enforced for the majority of zones but not system-validated.
score_4_desc: FIFO compliance runs at 85-95%, system-guided for putaway and picking across most zones.
score_5_desc: FIFO compliance exceeds 95%, system-enforced at putaway and picking with exceptions flagged automatically.

score_1_desc: Inventory accuracy (system vs. physical stock) runs under 90%, with no regular cycle-count process.
score_2_desc: Inventory accuracy runs at 90-95%, checked via periodic/ad hoc cycle counts.
score_3_desc: Inventory accuracy runs at 95-98%, checked via periodic cycle counts on a defined schedule.
score_4_desc: Inventory accuracy runs at 98-99.5%, checked via weekly cycle counts with variance root-caused.
score_5_desc: Inventory accuracy exceeds 99.5%, maintained via continuous/perpetual cycle counting with real-time variance alerts.

score_1_desc: Expiry loss exceeds 3% of inventory value/sales, not reconciled against FEFO compliance.
score_2_desc: Expiry loss runs at 2-3%.
score_3_desc: Expiry loss runs at 1-2%, tracked monthly but not yet linked to FEFO compliance.
score_4_desc: Expiry loss runs at 0.5-1%, reviewed monthly against FEFO compliance to close the loop.
score_5_desc: Expiry loss is held under 0.5%, tracked in real time and directly reconciled against FEFO/FIFO compliance.

subpoint_name: Labor Productivity - UPMH (Units per Manhour) vs. Target
score_1_desc: UPMH runs below 70% of the defined facility target, or no target is set at all.
score_2_desc: UPMH runs at 70-85% of target.
score_3_desc: UPMH runs at 85-95% of target, tracked weekly by function.
score_4_desc: UPMH runs at 95-105% of target, tracked weekly by function against defined targets.
score_5_desc: UPMH consistently runs at or above 105% of target, tracked weekly with continuous improvement.

subpoint_name: Labor Productivity - Orders per Manhour vs. Target
score_1_desc: Orders-per-manhour runs below 70% of the defined facility target, or no target is set at all.
score_2_desc: Orders-per-manhour runs at 70-85% of target.
score_3_desc: Orders-per-manhour runs at 85-95% of target, tracked weekly by function.
score_4_desc: Orders-per-manhour runs at 95-105% of target, tracked weekly against defined targets.
score_5_desc: Orders-per-manhour consistently runs at or above 105% of target, tracked weekly with continuous improvement.

score_1_desc: Labor utilization (productive hours) runs under 60%.
score_2_desc: Labor utilization runs at 60-70%.
score_3_desc: Labor utilization runs at 70-80%, tracked weekly by function.
score_4_desc: Labor utilization runs at 80-90%, tracked weekly against defined targets.
score_5_desc: Labor utilization exceeds 90%, tracked weekly with continuous improvement.

score_1_desc: Absenteeism exceeds 10%, not linked to staffing-variance root cause.
score_2_desc: Absenteeism runs at 7-10%, tracked but not analyzed.
score_3_desc: Absenteeism runs at 5-7%, tracked daily and reviewed as one driver of staffing variance.
score_4_desc: Absenteeism runs at 3-5%, tracked daily with a defined threshold and reviewed alongside attrition.
score_5_desc: Absenteeism is held under 3%, tracked daily and reviewed jointly with attrition and gig-supply risk as the standing staffing-variance root-cause set.

subpoint_name: Inward Accuracy (Actual Arrived Qty vs. Indent)
score_1_desc: Inward quantity deviates from Indent by more than 25%, with no reconciled tracking.
score_2_desc: Inward deviates from Indent by 15-25%, tracked in aggregate only.
score_3_desc: Inward deviates from Indent by 10-15%, reconciled daily for FnV/dry categories.
score_4_desc: Inward deviates from Indent by 5-10%, reconciled daily with variance root-caused monthly.
score_5_desc: Inward deviates from Indent by under 5%, reconciled in real time as part of the daily planning-cycle KPI set.

subpoint_name: Dispatched Accuracy (Actual Dispatched Qty vs. Plan)
score_1_desc: Dispatched quantity deviates from the plan by more than 25%, with no reconciled tracking.
score_2_desc: Dispatched deviates from plan by 15-25%, tracked in aggregate only.
score_3_desc: Dispatched deviates from plan by 10-15%, reconciled daily for FnV/dry categories.
score_4_desc: Dispatched deviates from plan by 5-10%, reconciled daily with variance root-caused monthly.
score_5_desc: Dispatched deviates from plan by under 5%, reconciled in real time alongside fill rate as part of the daily planning-cycle KPI set.

score_1_desc: Facility throughput under 60% of category benchmark (below 2.4 units/sq ft for FnV, or below 13.5-15 units/sq ft for dry storage).
score_2_desc: Throughput at 60-75% of benchmark.
score_3_desc: Throughput at 75-90% of benchmark (approximately 3-3.6 units/sq ft FnV, 17-20 units/sq ft dry).
score_4_desc:
Throughput at 90-100% of benchmark (4 units/sq ft FnV, 22.5-25 units/sq ft dry).
Outbound dispatch capacity validated at approximately 4x warehouse area.
score_5_desc:
Throughput consistently at or above benchmark.
Dispatch capacity engineered and validated at exactly 4x warehouse area (e.g., a 50,000 sq ft facility supporting 200,000-unit dispatch capacity), reviewed quarterly.

score_1_desc:
Layout not benchmarked against SPR/MTR design standards.
Storage-area ratio undefined or deviates over 70% from the 50-60% norm.
score_2_desc:
Partial benchmarking.
Storage ratio in the 60-70% band (too high, indicating processing-area shortfall) or below 40%.
score_3_desc:
Storage area at 50-60% of total footprint per design norm.
Aisle widths (~10 ft) and beam lengths (~2.4m) mostly conform to standard.
score_4_desc:
Full conformance to SPR/MTR specifications (aisle width, 100mm overhang, 3-4 ft sprinkler clearance) with storage ratio at 50-55%, or up to 60% for high-inventory/smaller-city sites.
Density near 22.5 units/sq ft.
score_5_desc: Layout fully optimized, including narrow-aisle configurations where applicable, at 22.5 units/sq ft density with 100% spec conformance and storage ratio precisely tuned to inventory-days requirement.

score_1_desc:
0-2 of the 6 cost components (manpower, material supply, packaging, electricity, depreciation, rent) tracked.
No periodic review.
score_2_desc:
3 components tracked.
Reviewed annually.
score_3_desc:
4 components tracked.
Reviewed quarterly.
score_4_desc:
5 components tracked.
Reviewed monthly, feeding into cost-per-unit optimization actions.
score_5_desc: All 6 components tracked, reviewed monthly or more frequently, with a documented cost-per-unit trend showing continuous reduction.

subpoint_name: Project Planning & Governance (Charter, Timeline, Cost Control)
score_1_desc:
No formal project charter, scope definition, or Gantt chart is used for planning/execution.
Timelines and budgets are not documented.
Delivery is tracked informally, with over 50% of projects (of any type - warehouse design/expansion, systems rollout, process change, etc.) running behind schedule or over budget with no visibility into the cause.
score_2_desc:
A basic project charter (scope/objective) is drafted for under 40% of projects.
No Gantt chart or formal milestone timeline is maintained.
Schedule or cost overrun exceeds 30% on the majority of tracked projects.
score_3_desc:
A project charter (scope, objective, stakeholders, budget) and a Gantt chart with defined milestones are used for 40-70% of projects.
Milestone/timeline adherence is reviewed periodically (e.g., monthly), but cost tracking against budget is inconsistent.
Schedule or cost overrun is in the 15-30% band.
score_4_desc:
A project charter and Gantt chart with milestone-level timelines are mandatory and used for 70-95% of projects.
Progress and cost are reviewed on a defined cadence (e.g., weekly) against the charter baseline.
Schedule/cost overrun held under 15%, with variances root-caused.
score_5_desc:
Over 95% of projects (irrespective of type) are governed by a formal charter and Gantt chart with baselined milestones, tracked in real time against a defined ownership/RACI matrix.
Over 90% of projects are delivered on time and within the approved budget (schedule/cost overrun under 5%), with lessons-learned closed out post-project.

score_1_desc: Cost per order runs more than 20% over the approved budget/benchmark, with no cost-per-order view tracked alongside cost-per-unit.
score_2_desc: Cost per order runs 10-20% over budget/benchmark.
score_3_desc: Cost per order runs within 10% of budget/benchmark, tracked quarterly alongside cost-per-unit.
score_4_desc: Cost per order runs at or below budget/benchmark, tracked monthly alongside cost-per-unit.
score_5_desc: Cost per order runs consistently below budget/benchmark with a documented downward trend, tracked monthly or more frequently.

score_1_desc: Utility cost per sqft runs more than 20% over the approved budget/benchmark, with no per-sqft normalization tracked.
score_2_desc: Utility cost per sqft runs 10-20% over budget/benchmark.
score_3_desc: Utility cost per sqft runs within 10% of budget/benchmark, tracked quarterly.
score_4_desc: Utility cost per sqft runs at or below budget/benchmark, tracked monthly.
score_5_desc: Utility cost per sqft runs consistently below budget/benchmark with a documented downward trend, tracked monthly or more frequently.

score_1_desc: Shrinkage cost exceeds 2% of sales, not reconciled with the volume-based shrinkage metric (A4.4).
score_2_desc: Shrinkage cost runs at 1.5-2% of sales.
score_3_desc: Shrinkage cost runs at 1-1.5% of sales, tracked quarterly.
score_4_desc: Shrinkage cost runs at 0.5-1% of sales, tracked monthly and reconciled against the volume-based shrinkage metric.
score_5_desc: Shrinkage cost is held under 0.5% of sales, tracked monthly or more frequently with a documented downward trend.

score_1_desc:
0% of inbound FnV volume routed through a collection center.
All sourcing goes direct to the main warehouse.
score_2_desc: Under 20% of volume routed via a collection center.
score_3_desc: 20-50% of volume via a collection center, reducing first-mile disruption.
score_4_desc: 50-80% of volume via a collection center, with a defined sorting/grading/packing split.
score_5_desc:
Over 80% of volume via a collection center.
A fully optimized first-mile network measurably reducing cost-per-unit quarter-on-quarter.

score_1_desc:
Under 50% of collection-center dispatches meet the 3:00 PM cutoff.
Frequent arrivals past 9:00 PM.
score_2_desc: 50-70% adherence to the 3:00 PM dispatch / 9:00 PM arrival cutoffs.
score_3_desc:
70-85% adherence.
Material typically arrives by 8-9 PM, packing completed by 11:30 PM.
score_4_desc:
85-95% adherence.
Arrival consistently by 7-8 PM, enabling processing completion by 12:00 AM and FnV dispatch by 1:00 PM.
score_5_desc: Over 95% adherence to the full cutoff chain (3 PM dispatch, 7-8 PM arrival, 12 AM processing complete, 1 PM FnV dispatch), tracked daily on an SLA dashboard.

score_1_desc:
No defined processing split between collection center and warehouse.
Allocation decided ad hoc daily.
score_2_desc: Split defined loosely (e.g., partial processing at collection center) but not documented as a fixed percentage.
score_3_desc: Split formally defined as a fixed percentage (e.g., 70% at collection center / 30% at warehouse) and followed on over 70% of days.
score_4_desc: Defined split followed on over 90% of days, reviewed monthly against volume and cost-per-unit impact.
score_5_desc: Split optimized and reviewed quarterly, followed on over 95% of days, with a documented cost/productivity rationale for the chosen ratio.

score_1_desc:
Unloading productivity not benchmarked by load type (packed vs bulk).
No target set.
score_2_desc:
Productivity tracked in aggregate only, below benchmark (under 400 units/person/hour packed.
Under 4 pallets/person/hour bulk).
score_3_desc: Productivity at benchmark for one load type only: 500 units/person/hour for packed material, or 5 pallets (125 crates)/person/hour for bulk - not both.
score_4_desc:
Productivity at benchmark for both load types (500 units/person/hour packed.
5 pallets or 125 crates/person/hour bulk), tracked daily.
score_5_desc: Productivity consistently at or above benchmark for both load types, tracked in real time, with variance-driven staffing adjustments.

score_1_desc:
No defined/target SLA for picking and allocation (benchmark: ~600 units/person/hour).
No defined physical staging zones, leading to congestion.
Allocation and holding material share the same physical zone with no clear demarcation.
No structured stacking/arrangement method for crates.
No defined dump/reject area within the staging zone.
score_2_desc:
Picking SLA is tracked for under 30% of shifts against the ~600 units/person/hour benchmark.
Wave Staging, Holding, and Reject/Dump zones are informally identified but frequently overlap.
Crate stacking in staging has no defined method.
A dump/reject corner exists but has no clearance routine.
score_3_desc:
Picking SLA is tracked for 30-60% of shifts.
Wave Staging, Holding, and Reject/Dump zones are marked with reduced but still occasional overlap.
A dump/reject corner has a clearance routine that is followed inconsistently.
A maximum days-of-holding (DoH) target for held material is defined but not consistently tracked.
score_4_desc:
Picking SLA is tracked for 60-90% of shifts and mostly at benchmark.
Wave Staging, Holding, and Reject/Dump zones are distinctly marked with no overlap on 70-95% of days.
The dump/reject corner follows a timed clearance SOP.
DoH SLA for holding material is tracked and mostly met.
score_5_desc:
Picking SLA is tracked for over 90% of shifts and consistently meets/exceeds the ~600 units/person/hour benchmark.
Wave Staging, Holding, and Reject/Dump zones are distinctly marked with zero overlap.
The dump/reject corner's timed clearance SOP is followed with zero aged-waste incidents.
DoH SLA for holding material is met on over 95% of days, reviewed as part of routine floor governance.

score_1_desc:
No defined SLA for dispatch/loading.
System allocation and physical allocation happen independently and out of sync, resulting in inventory mismatches at receiving hubs.
score_2_desc:
A loading SLA is defined (benchmark: ~2,500 units/person/hour) but tracked for under 30% of dispatches.
System and physical allocation are reconciled only after the fact, with inventory mismatches at hubs still common.
score_3_desc:
Loading SLA is tracked for 30-60% of dispatches against the ~2,500 units/person/hour benchmark.
Scanner-based allocation is used for some dispatches, but system and physical completion are not always simultaneous, leaving residual hub-level mismatches.
score_4_desc:
Loading SLA is tracked for 60-90% of dispatches and mostly at benchmark.
Scanner-based allocation with simultaneous system and physical completion is standard for the majority of dispatches, reducing hub-level inventory mismatches to occasional exceptions.
score_5_desc:
Loading SLA is tracked for over 90% of dispatches and consistently meets/exceeds the ~2,500 units/person/hour benchmark.
100% of allocations are scanner-based with simultaneous system and physical completion, eliminating hub-level inventory mismatches.
Evaluated as a standing criterion in every facility diagnostic, not a one-off, site-specific observation.
